EmailTemplate.subject: Thank you for your interest in the PhD in biological design
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Thank you for your interest in the biological design PhD program at Arizona State University. This innovative, interdisciplinary degree is designed to develop a new type of scientist — one equipped with both specialized expertise and the ability to identify solutions for context-specific problems. The research emphasis focuses on projects that contribute directly to solutions for important societal challenges.
The program features include:
an individualized program of study that teaches a team approach rotations through multiple research labs during the first year of study opportunities to collaborate with faculty and students from across the university faculty who encourage interdisciplinary research that is entrepreneurial and use-focused
Applications for fall admission should be submitted by Dec. 15 for priority review. In addition to the general admission requirements, applicants must submit the following to the Graduate College:
an online application official GRE scores TOEFL scores, if applicable resume or curriculum vitae a statement of purpose three letters of recommendation
Further information and instructions regarding how to apply can be found here.
There are no minimum GRE test scores required to gain entrance into the program, but scores should be competitive to increase an applicant’s likelihood of acceptance. The average GPA of admitted applicants this past year was 3.80, while the average GRE sub scores were 152, 158 and 3.8 for verbal, quantitative and analytical, respectively. The average TOEFL score for admitted students is 100. View English proficiency requirements online.
With faculty mentors and a personalized program of study, our students become part of a vibrant research community.
Sincerely,
